slides.title: Investigate, propose, authorize
slides.thesis: These are separate operations, not stages that imply automatic permission to change production.
rows: Read connected telemetry and change context.
Produce a diagnosis and mitigation proposal.
Use the separate directed-action gate for an eligible mutation.
slides.notes: Open with the distinction the team must preserve during an incident: analysis can run with read access, a proposal remains advice, and execution needs the appropriate configured and approved path. The guide covers environment inspection, incident operations, reliability recommendations, custom automation and preview release assessment. It does not claim that every account or source is connected, or that the agent replaces the incident commander.

slides.title: Know which object you are configuring
slides.thesis: Scope, work, context and execution are not the same object.
rows: Which problem and interval are being analyzed?
Which tools and context can this run use?
What is always loaded, selected or recalled?
slides.notes: Use the object model to prevent configuration errors. Registering an integration is not the same as associating it with the operational space. A Chat exchange is not necessarily a formal investigation. A custom agent definition is not an execution result. When someone says the agent knows the environment, ask which retained representation is involved, how recently it was refreshed, and whether the current run could actually read it.

slides.title: The functional map
slides.thesis: Group by product responsibility; do not label an example incident as a capability.
rows: Incident record and separate quality assessment
Run a configured custom agent; channel delivery
Review code; test a running UI/API
Readiness report or executed test evidence
slides.notes: Explain why these areas are separate. Querying a metric is not an incident diagnosis. Creating a recommendation is not deploying it. A recurring health report is a configured task using selected functions, not a universal built-in report. Release readiness examines a change; release testing exercises a running application. The full report provides operation-level inputs and boundaries, so this slide is a map rather than the whole reference.

slides.title: Accessible evidence is not necessarily inspected evidence
slides.thesis: Trace a material conclusion back through the query, source and permission boundary.
rows: Alarm/resource ID; account; region; UTC interval
Associated integration and effective role permissions
Actual tool query, returned timestamps and identifiers
Hypothesis supported by the current result
slides.callout: Denied access, missing data and a genuine empty query result must remain distinct.
slides.notes: Take one claimed cause and work backwards. Was the right log group queried? Was the interval correct? Did the result contain the affected resource? Did the source return no records, or did the call fail? Only after those checks should the conclusion be weighed. This is a proposed evidence-review discipline, not a guarantee of how every agent response is formatted. The same discipline applies to a topology map: inspect freshness and identifiers before assuming it describes the current deployment.

slides.title: Triage and investigation controls have different effects
slides.thesis: Choose the control that changes the intended object, not merely the visible conversation.
rows: Assuming a repeated alarm always has the old cause
Combine with, or separate from, related work
Treating temporal proximity as proof of common cause
Suppress, or restore, investigation of an event
Suppressing critical alerts with a broad maintenance rule
Redirect, continue or branch the analysis
Losing the original hypothesis and evidence trail
slides.notes: The operator should be able to explain why an event was linked or skipped. A maintenance exception is an operational policy that needs exact scope, not a generic request to ignore noise. For an investigation already underway, steering adds information; for an alternative line, a fork preserves the original. These controls manage the analysis lifecycle. They neither silence the originating monitoring system nor confer authority to change resources.

slides.title: Diagnosis, Review and feedback are different evidence
slides.thesis: A quality assessment reads the record; it does not rerun the incident against the environment.
rows: A measured accuracy improvement from one submission
slides.callout: Review Accuracy can be not applicable when no reference diagnosis exists on the linked incident.
slides.notes: A review can assess grounding and completeness, but it is constrained by the same recorded evidence. Explain the special case where Accuracy is not applicable: the grader has no established root cause to compare with. Corrective feedback is a separate operator input. Current documentation connects it to reflections for later investigations, but seeing a reflection is not evidence that a later run retrieved it or reached the right conclusion.

slides.title: A proposed mitigation has no execution authority
slides.thesis: Directed actions add a controlled mutation path; they do not remove the need to verify recovery.
rows: Registered elevated account role or allowed mutating tool
Individual operation, parameters and target in Chat
API result, audit event and independent service state
slides.callout: Release testing sends application writes through a different execution path.
slides.notes: Walk through the gates in order. A broad role is not permission to skip the Chat approval, and a Chat approval does not override service-level prohibitions. A custom MCP classification is metadata; inspect the backend's real privileges. For the demonstration, do not perform a production change. Show a prepared approval and rejected-action case, then explain the additional recovery metric needed after any actual approved mutation.

slides.title: What persists after an incident?
slides.thesis: Retained context, generated environment knowledge and correction records have distinct lifecycles.
rows: A historical hypothesis to test against current telemetry
Corrective feedback on a failed investigation
A lesson associated with the monitor, not proof of recall
Derived context with a timestamp and update conditions
Only useful when described, active and attached as needed
slides.notes: Avoid the phrase learns from everything. Describe an inspectable object instead: its store, content, version and last update. Current documentation maintains learned environment knowledge as memory, while older cached pages describe learned skills. Monitor and tool-use stores have different update cadences. The underlying model-training implementation is not established by these documents. The practical question is whether relevant, accurate context was available and actually used in the later task.

slides.title: Enable and verify memory deliberately
slides.thesis: Presence, activation, retrieval and correctness are four different checks.
rows: Knowledge → Memories: content, version and timestamp
Activate the intended store; attach it to the custom agent
Learning History/Triggers and available run read evidence
Compare the recalled cause with present telemetry
slides.callout: Managed stores are read-only to custom agents; attached custom stores can be written.
slides.notes: A new custom agent has no memory access until stores are attached. The built-in incident behavior and custom-agent attachments should not be conflated. Demonstrate the proposed verification process with a prepared store: identify what should be recalled, inspect the later run where evidence is visible, and state unverified when the interface does not expose that read. Deactivate misleading context while correcting it; do not delete the incident's source record.

slides.title: A scheduled report is a configured program of work
slides.thesis: The custom-agent facility provides execution; the team supplies the task definition and acceptance rule.
rows: Resource scope, rule and output contract
Vague analysis with no resource-level result
Future runs continue after one task is cancelled
slides.notes: Use the report's configuration-check procedure as an example. A reliable check needs an explicit comparison against an observed field and three possible results: compliant, non-compliant or unknown. Test the unknown case intentionally. Do not create a schedule merely because the agent can produce a plausible report once. Review the selected toolbox and run history; pausing a trigger and cancelling an invocation are separate controls.

slides.title: Release review and release testing are not interchangeable
slides.thesis: One analyzes the change; the other interacts with the deployed application.
rows: Target profile, test intent and credentials
Inspect operational risk in the change
Explore UI/API behavior with real requests
Executed test results and reproduction evidence
Not a deployment gate without integration
Can create, modify or delete application data
slides.notes: Both require feature-level availability checks and are documented in us-east-1 during preview. A report saying Block does not automatically stop a pipeline. An application test may send notifications or process payments if the environment allows those effects. Require safe staging data and explicit target authorization. Do not reuse the directed-action approval model as a claim that every application request needs operator confirmation.

slides.title: Demonstration: challenge a recurring diagnosis
slides.thesis: Use prepared evidence to show the decisions; do not promise an eight-minute end-to-end investigation.
slides.notes: Follow the five timed steps in the report. The presenter needs a permission-cleared incident record, prior memory, actual source-query output and a prepared mitigation proposal. No live AWS work has been executed for this documentation. If a live environment is available, retain the same decision sequence and switch to prepared evidence rather than waiting for an unbounded run. The audience should see a material claim challenged, not only a successful agent response.

slides.title: Operational acceptance is evidence, not fluency
slides.thesis: Start with a bounded service and retain unresolved gaps explicitly.
rows: Scope and source queries match the incident
Required telemetry is denied or missing
A proposal identifies target and recovery test
One run versus its recurring trigger
The report fabricates an all-clear result
Preview tests have a safe target
Real external side effects are possible
slides.notes: Close with decisions the team can make immediately: one service scope, one useful investigation procedure, one source-reconciliation check and a separate mutation approval policy. These are proposed adoption controls, not measured outcomes. The detailed report includes configuration, evidence sources and known documentation differences. Questions and any live setup work are outside the timed programme.

slides.title: Match the assessment to the evidence required
slides.thesis: A design statement, a source finding and a reproduced runtime exploit answer different questions.
rows: Does this code contain a security issue?
Can this issue be reproduced on this target?
slides.notes: Introduce the assessment boundaries rather than a broad security promise. The requested product name is retained; the current documentation identifies it as part of AWS Continuum. Code review, design review and threat modeling are preview. Penetration testing has a separate availability and billing model. The presentation concentrates on selecting the right operation and interpreting its result.

slides.title: Four groups of functions
slides.thesis: Separate analysis, runtime testing, repair proposals and evidence management.
rows: Control assessment or modeled attack scenario
Full scan; diff scan; simulated validation
Code finding with separate validation state
Observed test evidence against a target
slides.notes: A full scan and a diff scan differ in scope, not in whether the result is automatically true. Simulated validation adds an attempted exploit in a constructed environment; it is not a production test. Revalidation repeats selected previous findings and does not discover unrelated issues. A proposed patch and a report are outputs requiring review, not proof that the vulnerability was removed.

slides.title: Requirement review is not threat modeling
slides.thesis: Use a fixed criterion to evaluate a control; use a threat model to reason about attacker paths.
rows: Scope documents, source context or both
What can cross this trust boundary?
slides.notes: Use an authorization example. A design may state that object access is restricted to the owner but omit where the decision is enforced. Requirement review should expose the evidence gap. Threat modeling asks how a different identity could reach the object and which trust boundary would be crossed. Neither proves an exploit succeeds. Review the architecture model before prioritizing its generated threats.

slides.title: Requirement packs are controlled inputs
slides.thesis: Generated requirements must be reviewed before they govern new assessments.
rows: Enable the pack for new design/code reviews
Record the criteria used for each run
slides.callout: Uploading replacement documents regenerates the entire custom pack, including manual requirements.
slides.notes: The control is more specific than upload our policy. Give each requirement an observable meaning and a clear non-applicability condition. Packs are shared across Agent Spaces, so an edit can affect more than the current review. Existing results are not recomputed when a pack changes. A framework-oriented pack helps identify relevant requirements; it does not certify compliance.

slides.title: Choose full-source or differential analysis intentionally
slides.thesis: A changed-code review still needs surrounding source context.
rows: Repository branch or complete S3 source ZIP
PR change or source ZIP plus unified diff
Revision, artifact and trigger must match
No returned findings for that completed scope
Not a baseline assurance for unchanged code
slides.notes: A skipped trigger, a failed preflight and a completed clean review must be visibly distinct. Before reviewing a finding, identify the exact source revision. For a programmatic diff job, a patch alone does not provide the source context the service expects. For PR reviews, verify the configured publication permissions and the branch or label filters rather than inferring success from an absence of comments.

slides.title: Simulated validation has four different outcomes
slides.thesis: Do not collapse non-reproduction, failed execution and no attempt into 'safe'.
rows: Exploit succeeded in the simulated environment
Does the evidence match the affected path?
Attempt did not reproduce under these conditions
Attempt was inconclusive due to an error
No completed validation for this finding
slides.notes: State the environment prerequisite before showing results: the application must fit the supported simulated setup. A private dependency or startup failure is not evidence against a source finding. Conversely, a confirmed exploit should still be examined for its actual path and conditions. The result is stronger than a bare static assertion but remains bounded by the environment in which it was produced.

slides.title: A runtime test needs four independent permissions
slides.thesis: Control of the domain does not grant unrestricted application access or eliminate side effects.
rows: Verified, associated domain and authorized environment
Reachable endpoint, configured private path if needed
Included paths, exclusions, risk classes and limits
slides.callout: Use disposable staging data and disable real external effects before exploratory traffic.
slides.notes: Explain which problem each configuration solves. A verified domain can still be unreachable. A reachable login page does not prove authenticated endpoints are exercised. A powerful test account can also produce misleading authorization coverage if the real risk concerns a less privileged user. Match identities and data to the specific behavior the team needs to assess and monitor target-side logs.

slides.title: Retesting a finding is not a new penetration test
slides.thesis: Deploy the fix to the original target before interpreting a revalidation result.
rows: Selected risk surface of the application
Run tasks and newly discovered findings
Original finding plus separate retest history
Application test evidence for the patched build
slides.callout: Resolved means not reproduced in that revalidation; it does not establish whole-application security.
slides.notes: Use the same target and current valid credentials. Check the build identity at the target rather than the branch containing the fix. A revalidation can be narrowly useful after a small repair, but a wider change may introduce other paths that only a broader test or application regression suite covers. Retain the original evidence rather than replacing it with a new status label.

slides.title: Do not confuse four finding attributes
slides.thesis: Each attribute answers a different question.
rows: How serious could the impact be?
How confident is the agent in this finding?
Was an exploit attempt made and reproduced?
How has the organization handled it?
slides.notes: Use one high-impact, unvalidated item and one lower-impact confirmed item. Neither can be prioritized on a single attribute alone. Inspect default filters before reporting totals. A report can include organization-authored notes; they must remain distinguishable from the service's assessment. Manual risk acceptance and a fixed vulnerability are different operational outcomes.

slides.title: A repair proposal needs behavior tests
slides.thesis: Generating the diff is not the completion criterion.
rows: Source path, intended rule and proposed patch
Code rereview or target revalidation as appropriate
slides.callout: A patch that blocks legitimate access can remove the exploit and still be an unacceptable fix.
slides.notes: The source connection may support a PR or a downloadable diff depending on the route. Do not generalize that into automatic merge or deployment. The developer must preserve intended behavior while enforcing the control. For an ownership check, test both the owner and a different identity. The original assessment type determines what evidence is needed after the repair.

slides.title: Demonstration: an authorization change before merge
slides.thesis: Inspect revision, trigger, source path and validation state before judging the patch.
slides.notes: Use the five one-minute steps in the procedure. Prepare a permission-cleared PR, its review record and positive/negative test output. This is a result-reading and decision exercise, not a promise that a scan completes in five minutes. The presenter must show why a finding is accepted, rejected or left unresolved rather than presenting an unexamined agent recommendation.

slides.title: Demonstration: verify a deployed fix
slides.thesis: A valid non-reproduction requires the patched build, functioning authentication and the intended endpoint.
slides.notes: Show the original finding, the patched target and a prepared revalidation run. Contrast an active vulnerability with valid non-reproduction and with an authentication failure. Then show the application owner's allowed/denied regression results. The conclusion should name the specific finding and build, not state that the system is secure. Use prepared evidence if live prerequisites are absent.

slides.title: An assessment record must preserve its boundary
slides.thesis: Make the scope of a conclusion visible to the next engineer.
slides.notes: The output should allow another engineer to understand what was tested without reconstructing the session. Report filters, task limits and missing access are part of the assessment boundary. This is a proposed record-keeping standard, not a claim that a generated report is sufficient for every audit. Questions and live account setup are outside the timed presentation.

slides.title: Keep source data, explanation and action separate
slides.thesis: The service retrieves and interprets cost information; it does not make every explanation or recommendation an established fact.
rows: Scoped explanation, report or recommendation summary
slides.notes: The entire service remains preview. The presentation follows the data from its source to a reviewable result and then to a separately controlled publication. Cost Explorer supplies billing data; Cost Optimization Hub and Compute Optimizer supply optimization recommendations. A recommendation, forecast and actual saving are different kinds of information and must remain visibly distinct.

slides.title: The functional map follows the source of truth
slides.thesis: Do not turn categories of recommendations into invented agent optimization engines.
rows: Cost Explorer and permitted billing tools
Scoped source data and detector event
Create/comment in Jira; post to Slack
Actual issue, comment or channel message
slides.notes: This map separates functions by what they operate on and return. An anomaly event comes from a detector; the agent investigates it. A rightsizing candidate comes from an optimization source; the agent can summarize it. Report generation changes representation, not the underlying numbers. Publication is an external write whose result should be checked in the destination.

slides.title: A cost comparison starts with a query contract
slides.thesis: Reconciliation is impossible until the scopes match.
rows: Retain the exact metric and units
slides.notes: Use this contract before requesting an explanation. An increase may result from a different query rather than a change in the workload. This is why a chart or executive summary is not the first artifact to inspect. Reconcile the overall total and one material contributor against the same source settings, then investigate the remaining difference.

slides.title: Worked example: 200 becomes 244
slides.thesis: Synthetic teaching data: the 44 increase can be reconciled without claiming why it occurred.
slides.callout: Invented quantities and rates. Not AWS pricing, billing records or a measured agent result.
slides.notes: Compute the totals explicitly. Under the quantity-first convention, the quantity contribution is 200 additional units times the old rate, or 20. The rate contribution is the new quantity times the rate increase, or 24. The contributions total 44. Other conventions can allocate the interaction term differently. The numbers establish the decomposition, not whether a deployment or discount change caused it. A total-only fixture could not establish this split.

slides.title: Anomaly detection is not causal proof
slides.thesis: Trace the suspected cause to the affected resource and changed usage.
rows: Anomaly ID, monitor and affected interval
CloudTrail or deployment event, if accessible
Did this event change this resource's measured usage?
slides.callout: A correlated event is a hypothesis. Missing CloudTrail evidence is not proof that no change occurred.
slides.notes: Keep the anomaly amount separate from the broader period comparison. If a deployment occurs near the increase, test whether the increase preceded it or affected resources outside its scope. If the required source is unavailable, report the gap. The agent's investigative explanation is a starting point for the owner, not a definitive billing-causality verdict.

slides.title: Three numbers that must not be conflated
slides.thesis: Measured cost, forecast and recommendation estimates have different meanings.
rows: Source billing observation under a defined scope
Source model's estimate for a future interval
Control for demand and workload changes
slides.notes: Realized savings is a proposed measurement the team performs after an approved change, not a field inferred from a recommendation. A forecast is not a budget authorization. For commitments, coverage and utilization answer different questions: eligible usage covered versus purchased commitment used. A purchase decision needs explicit demand and term assumptions, not simply a desire to increase one percentage.

slides.title: Recommendation retrieval is not infrastructure optimization
slides.thesis: The agent contextualizes source-service recommendations; engineering owns implementation and measurement.
rows: The newest chat answer means new source analysis
Shows the actual change being proposed
A generic 'save money' summary is implementable
Every listed estimate can be added
slides.notes: Open the underlying recommendation before drafting work. Ask the workload owner whether the observed period included peak load and relevant redundancy constraints. Reject unsupported candidates rather than creating a large unowned backlog. The agent does not resize resources or buy commitments through the documented publishing actions. The subsequent engineering change should have its own authorization and regression plan.

slides.title: Context and memory change interpretation, not billing truth
slides.thesis: Owner mappings and reporting preferences must not silently alter measured totals.
rows: Persists preferences and corrections per agent
Not the same as durable cross-session memory
No individual deletion during documented preview
slides.notes: Use a mapping example with a known account and an unknown account. The unknown one must remain visible and its cost must remain in the total. Context files are visible to users with access to the agent; they should not carry sensitive personal information. A correction can affect later interpretation, but it does not rewrite the underlying billing data or establish a model-training mechanism.

slides.title: A task is one run; an automation creates runs
slides.thesis: Cancelling current work and stopping future work are separate operations.
slides.callout: Disable the automation for future runs; cancel an already-running task separately.
slides.notes: Test the analysis as an on-demand task before making it recurring. For event automation, confirm the existing monitor, matching conditions and required EventBridge permissions. A task can fail because of missing source access or an expired publishing credential. The operational owner must inspect those failures; a schedule is not a guarantee that the intended report arrived or was complete.

slides.title: Publishing controls are action-specific
slides.thesis: Do not describe all writes as requiring approval.
slides.callout: Jira cannot set assignee/priority/status here. Slack is posting-only during preview.
slides.notes: The account-level OAuth integration and the per-agent project or channel connection are both required. A Jira owner in a context file does not make the integration an assignee editor. Slack does not accept commands or respond to mentions through this preview connection. Review destination audience before enabling unattended publication; waiting for Jira approval does not hold back a separate Slack post.

slides.title: Demonstration: reconcile before explaining
slides.thesis: Use the synthetic fixture for arithmetic and prepared source evidence for interpretation.
slides.notes: Follow the five one-minute steps. The fixture is deliberately small so the audience can verify the calculation rather than trust a generated summary. State clearly that it is not a live billing query. Then show how a report should carry query scope, remaining residual and causal uncertainty. A deployment-cause conclusion requires evidence beyond the fixture.

slides.title: Demonstration: recommendation to reviewable work
slides.thesis: A ticket is a proposed change, not achieved savings.
slides.notes: Inspect one prepared recommendation and one overlapping alternative. Review the draft issue and identify fields that the integration cannot set. Show the approval boundary using a prepared example unless an authorized test project is actually connected. End with the measurement required after engineering independently approves and deploys the change.

slides.title: Acceptance requires a traceable numerical result
slides.thesis: A useful cost report makes both the arithmetic and the remaining uncertainty inspectable.
slides.notes: Close by asking which operational decision the report enables. If it cannot identify the cost scope, the evidence for a driver or the owner of a proposed change, more generated prose will not help. The complete reference contains configuration and lifecycle instructions. No savings, accuracy or productivity outcome has been measured for this documentation, and questions are outside the timed session.
